pattern: The approved architecture is a synthetic MedTech PMS pilot. Implementation approval does not authorize Azure deployment, real medical data or external transmissions.
implication: Prepare IaC only; default to private access and simulated transmissions. Require separate deployment and operational approval.

pattern: No subscription, existing Azure resource, region/SKU/model availability, quota or cost evidence was supplied. The environment-insights MCP tool is unavailable; no tenant scan was performed.
implication: Do not invent existing ARM IDs or deployment evidence. Treat region, capacity, identity bootstrap, access and cost as unverified deployment gates.

pattern: Model processing is EU-member-state-only. Current deployment-type docs include EFTA in the EU boundary while the privacy page uses EU-member-nations wording; neither DataZone nor a region label proves the requested boundary.
implication: Standard geography candidate only; no Global/DataZone/Developer fallback. AgentHost requires EU-Member-States and a canonical configuration-hash-bound review with actual processing countries. No legal/provider approval is inferred from hashing.

pattern: SQL is the authoritative business state with transactional audit/outbox/inbox; Blob stores evidence; Search is reconstructable. Durable uses separate Blob/Queue/Table storage and Operations is independent from agents.
implication: Separate identities and storage accounts, private endpoints and DNS for all three Durable services. Do not add a broker, AKS or Cosmos DB.

pattern: The allowed read-only application snapshot uses SDK 10.0.404 via global.json, Cohors.slnx, a React/Vite build and SQL integration tests requiring loopback COHORS_TEST_CONNECTION. The API serves static files and exposes /health/live and /health/ready.
implication: CI uses global.json, Node 22 LTS, the web lockfile and fresh real loopback SQL; no skipped suites. Confirmed target: cohors-api and separate cohors-agents on 8080, separate Flex code packages via OneDeploy. Exact identity, boundary-review and unsampled watchdog contracts are bound; full Linux/cloud integration remains unverified here.

pattern: Production WORM duration, externally protected SQL ledger digests and recovery acceptance are not approved or live verified.
implication: Create separated storage boundaries without locking retention. Gate digest publishing, retention activation and restore acceptance explicitly; never open storage firewalls to make digest export work.

pattern: The coordinator read the original requirements matrix and mapped 118 unique IDs (104 mandatory, 14 recommended); the source-availability gap is closed, not the implementation or acceptance gaps. Architecture source is now v0.3.
implication: L-01 requires object-specific retention rather than blanket raw-data WORM; L-03 requires audit, recovery and independent digest evidence; L-05 preserves need-to-know, encryption, minimization and the separate Privacy/EU gate. Application documentation and individual acceptance remain with Cohors-Pilot.
